profiles.name: Charles Shi
profiles.role: Needham & Company analyst at source time

current_role.title: Not independently reverified beyond latest cited call roster
current_role.access: Source-time identity only; do not imply current employment after this date.

profiles.scope: Reconcile legal and strategic narratives with the actual financial baseline
profiles.boundary: Two independently dated public call samples. These show questions asked, not a permanent philosophy, licensed model, forecast accuracy or investment performance. No recurring personal-pattern certification.

readings.locator: printed pp.8–9; operator introduction and Charles Shi questions
readings.summary: Shi probes litigation assumptions in revenue forecasts and whether a stable royalty mix masks absolute growth.
readings.attribution: Questions by Shi; royalty outlook and explanation by Jason Child/Rene Haas.

readings.locator: printed pp.12–13; Charles Shi questions and follow-up
readings.summary: Shi asks what subsidy fairness means and distinguishes factory-support R&D from developing new process nodes.
readings.attribution: Questions by Shi; subsidy/R&D assertions by TSMC management.

card_ideas.title: Legal news versus the embedded forecast
card_ideas.model: Rebuild the pre-event forecast before assigning an incremental earnings effect to litigation news.
card_ideas.variables_units: royalty rate (%), eligible sales ($), renewal date, forecast assumption
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Revise forecast only when modeled contract economics change.
card_ideas.counterexample: A legal loss can still alter bargaining leverage or future renewals even if near-term forecast assumed loss.
card_ideas.test: Compare dated pre-event assumptions with disclosed contract terms and subsequent royalty receipts.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: An industrial license dispute with unchanged near-term invoicing but uncertain renewal.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: A license firm forecasts $100m royalties assuming it loses a lawsuit. It then loses. What immediate revenue revision follows from this fact alone?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: Zero from that fact alone: the loss was in the baseline. Check changes to rates, duration, enforcement and renewal before revising.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: renewal prices may fall20% in two years. Separate present revenue from future risk.

card_ideas.title: A flat mix share can conceal rapid absolute growth
card_ideas.model: Separate component dollars from total-company denominator before diagnosing adoption stagnation.
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Use component revenue = share × comparable total; diagnose only after separating mix from scale.
card_ideas.counterexample: Flat share can still hide unit weakness when royalty rates rose.
card_ideas.test: Decompose units, rates, mix and denominator growth across comparable periods.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: Cloud premium-tier share remains flat as total usage doubles.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: Premium royalty share stays25% as total royalties rise from$100m to$140m. Has premium revenue stalled?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: No. It rises$25m→$35m,40%. Units and rates still need separating.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: premium rates rose50%. What can you infer about eligible sales?

card_ideas.title: R&D headcount is not autonomous technology capability
card_ideas.locator: pp.12–13, Charles Shi R&D question and follow-up
card_ideas.model: Map research scope, decision rights and deliverables before treating a local center as independent innovation capacity.
card_ideas.variables_units: engineers, budget ($), project scope, qualification milestones
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Claim capability only when local responsibility and validated deliverables support it.
card_ideas.counterexample: A small center may lead a critical module despite limited headcount.
card_ideas.test: Track ownership of process experiments, patents, qualification signoff and technology transfer.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: A packaging supplier announces a foreign design center.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: A foreign R&D center has1,000 engineers but only factory yield-support responsibility. Is it evidence of independent next-node development?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: No. Headcount does not establish design authority or deliverables. Seek experimental ownership, qualification responsibility and new-node outputs.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence:50engineers own a critical reusable process module. Reassess capability without treating headcount as the score.

gaps: No complete licensed research or frozen estimates obtained.

profiles.name: Arthur Lai

current_role.title: Not independently reverified beyond latest cited call roster
current_role.access: Source-time identity only; do not imply current employment after this date.

profiles.scope: Test where product boundaries change competitive and demand interpretations
profiles.boundary: Two independently dated public call samples. These show questions asked, not a permanent philosophy, licensed model, forecast accuracy or investment performance. No recurring personal-pattern certification.

readings.summary: Lai tests the competitive implications of an alternative packaging technology.
readings.attribution: Question premise is Lai’s; competitor benefits claimed in the answer belong to management.

readings.locator: printed pp.16–17; Arthur Lai two questions
readings.summary: Lai probes electricity constraints, backside-power adoption, and whether CPUs belong inside reported AI growth.
readings.attribution: Do not adopt the proposed power-to-adoption link; management rejects that causal shortcut.

card_ideas.title: A rival can unlock upstream sales
card_ideas.model: Compare profit lost in a constrained complement with upstream profit enabled by bottleneck relief.
card_ideas.variables_units: lost packaging units and margin, incremental wafers and margin
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Net effect changes sign when enabled upstream contribution exceeds lost downstream contribution.
card_ideas.counterexample: Alternative packaging also migrates wafer sourcing, reversing complementarity.
card_ideas.test: Observe compatible wafer orders, package share and customer qualification rather than headline market share.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: A networking vendor benefits when a rival removes a system integration bottleneck.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: Alternative packaging loses you$30m contribution but enables$50m upstream wafer contribution. What is the direct net effect before spillovers?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: +$20m. Keep the two layers and incremental baseline separate; then test whether wafer sourcing also migrates.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: half the enabled wafer orders switch supplier.

card_ideas.title: System scarcity does not identify the winning device technology
card_ideas.model: Require a workload and design constraint bridge between grid scarcity and adoption of a chip-level feature.
card_ideas.variables_units: facility MW, workload efficiency, redesign cost ($), schedule
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Adoption follows net system benefit and qualification feasibility, not scarcity alone.
card_ideas.counterexample: Cooling or software changes deliver the same benefit without silicon redesign.
card_ideas.test: Compare performance per watt under equal workload and redesign/qualification costs.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: Memory compression proposed as a cure for a site-power shortage.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: A datacenter lacks20MW. A new chip feature improves workload performance/W by10% but requires18months redesign. Does grid scarcity alone prove immediate adoption?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: No. Quantify workload-level savings, schedule, redesign cost and alternatives; the power constraint does not identify which intervention wins.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: software optimization delivers8% within one month.

card_ideas.title: Growth is meaningless without a stable category boundary
card_ideas.model: Maintain separate narrow and broad demand series with a reconciliation rather than silently enlarging a CAGR denominator.
card_ideas.variables_units: category revenue ($), base year, inclusion rules
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Compare growth only after restating both endpoints to the same definition.
card_ideas.counterexample: Dual-use products cannot be reliably allocated between categories.
card_ideas.test: Publish inclusion rules and sensitivity ranges for ambiguous allocation.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: Security software AI-labelled revenue expands by reclassifying legacy subscriptions.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: A category grows$10bn→$20bn. You add$5bn of dual-use CPUs only to the endpoint. Can you report150% comparable growth?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: No. Restate the starting period under the same category definition, or present old and expanded categories separately.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: only20–60% of CPU sales serve the named use case; use a range.

current_role.title: Not independently reverified beyond latest cited call roster
current_role.access: Source-time identity only; do not imply current employment after this date.

profiles.scope: Translate technology roadmaps and cross-component constraints into deployable output
profiles.boundary: Two independently dated public call samples. These show questions asked, not a permanent philosophy, licensed model, forecast accuracy or investment performance. No recurring personal-pattern certification.

readings.summary: Chen asks about chip mix and the maturity of glass-related packaging options.
readings.attribution: Questions by Chen; production timing is management testimony.

readings.summary: Chen connects chip demand to power, financing and component constraints, then questions capital productivity.
readings.attribution: No independent endorsement of management demand or profitability forecasts.

card_ideas.title: Orders versus fully deployable systems
card_ideas.model: Represent the deployment chain as matched components and funded energized capacity; identify the binding complement.
card_ideas.variables_units: chips, packages, memory capacity, powered MW, financing ($), dates
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Do not equate booked chips with deployed output when a required complement is unavailable.
card_ideas.counterexample: Customers build inventory ahead of an imminent bottleneck release without overbuilding.
card_ideas.test: Reconcile delivery cohorts against commissioning dates and inventory accumulation.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: An electrification supplier has orders but utility interconnection is delayed.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic:100servers are delivered, power supports60, and networking supports80. What upper bound is deployable now under one-unit-per-server assumptions?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: 60, assuming matching configurations and all other complements available. Orders alone do not establish deployed output.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: the next power milestone is delayed six months; examine inventory and financing.

card_ideas.title: A material roadmap needs qualification evidence
card_ideas.model: Distinguish material demonstration, pilot process, qualified product and economic high-volume production.
card_ideas.variables_units: yield (%), reliability passes, substrate cost ($), qualified packages
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Revenue ramp requires customer-qualified manufacturability, not a demonstration alone.
card_ideas.counterexample: A higher-cost material is viable for a limited high-value segment before mass adoption.
card_ideas.test: Require reliability, yield and customer release milestones at the proposed production date.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: A new optical interconnect material claims a rapid commercial ramp.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: A substrate passes a lab demonstration but has no customer reliability qualification. Should its full revenue ramp enter the base case?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: Not solely on the demonstration. Use milestone-conditioned scenarios and test qualification, yield and cost.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: one premium customer qualifies low-volume use; distinguish niche adoption from mass production.

card_ideas.title: More expensive equipment can improve capital productivity
card_ideas.model: Compare cost per qualified output and capital turns, separating equipment price from effective throughput.
card_ideas.variables_units: tool price ($), throughput, uptime, yield, revenue ($)
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Investment is productive only if risk-adjusted incremental cash return clears its capital cost.
card_ideas.counterexample: Higher throughput remains unused or requires costly complementary tooling.
card_ideas.test: Track utilization-adjusted throughput, qualified yield and cash conversion after installation.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: A battery factory upgrades to faster but more capital-intensive production tools.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: A tool costs20% more and produces40% more qualified output at equal utilization. How changes capital per output?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: 1.2/1.4=0.857, about14.3% lower. Still test uptime, demand, complementary investment and cash returns.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: utilization drops from90% to60%; recalculate effective output.

profiles.name: Haas Liu
profiles.role: BofA Securities analyst at source time

current_role.title: Not independently reverified beyond latest cited call roster
current_role.access: Source-time identity only; do not imply current employment after this date.

profiles.scope: Separate spending drivers, competitive spillovers and process-learning economics
profiles.boundary: Two independently dated public call samples. These show questions asked, not a permanent philosophy, licensed model, forecast accuracy or investment performance. No recurring personal-pattern certification.

readings.summary: Liu separates demand from tool-price effects and tests whether packaging competition spreads upstream.
readings.attribution: Questions by Liu; management’s competitive response is not the analyst’s own conclusion.

readings.summary: Liu questions AI workload mix and the yield-learning cost of parallel process tracks.
readings.attribution: Questions are hypotheses; qualitative management reassurance is not independently verified yield data.

card_ideas.title: Deflate investment before inferring capacity
card_ideas.model: Decompose nominal capex into input inflation, asset mix and real capacity; avoid treating every spending increase as demand growth.
card_ideas.variables_units: capex ($), tool price index, asset mix, qualified throughput
card_ideas.decision_boundary: A demand inference requires evidence of added useful capacity after price and mix adjustment.
card_ideas.counterexample: A more expensive tool can increase output enough to lower unit capital cost.
card_ideas.test: Reconcile procurement prices, tool counts, yield and commissioning dates.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: Data-center capex rises because land and power equipment prices increase.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: Nominal equipment spending rises30%; comparable tool prices rise25% and mix is unchanged. What approximate physical acquisition growth?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: 1.30/1.25-1=4%. This is acquired inputs, not yet qualified productive capacity.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: tool mix shifts toward higher-throughput units; simple deflation no longer suffices.

card_ideas.title: Adjacent competition needs a migration mechanism
card_ideas.model: Test whether entry in one layer transfers customer control, IP or qualification to the adjacent layer.
card_ideas.variables_units: customer overlap, redesign costs ($), qualification time, margin by layer
card_ideas.decision_boundary: Predict spillover only where switching and capability pathways are evidenced.
card_ideas.counterexample: An open interface allows one layer to compete without changing the supplier of another.
card_ideas.test: Track joint design wins, platform dependence and actual sourcing migrations.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: Storage software competitor enters appliances but does not own drive manufacturing.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: A competitor gains30% packaging share. What evidence is missing before predicting30% wafer-share loss?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: A mechanism connecting packaging adoption to wafer substitution: design compatibility, process capability, customer decisions, switching costs and qualification. Equal shares cannot be assumed.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence: one package platform mandates a paired wafer process; bound the affected segment.

card_ideas.title: Two process tracks may fragment learning
card_ideas.model: Model transferable learning versus track-specific defects and complexity rather than extrapolating one aggregate yield curve.
card_ideas.variables_units: volume per track, die area, defect density, yield (%), cost per good die ($)
card_ideas.decision_boundary: A shared learning assumption needs evidence of process commonality and cross-track improvement.
card_ideas.counterexample: Distinct tracks share most unit processes and retain learning economies.
card_ideas.test: Compare cohort yields and common process steps while controlling die size and product mix.
card_ideas.deadline: At the next relevant disclosure or qualification milestone; no analyst-specific deadline asserted.
card_ideas.transfer: An aircraft producer ramps two variants with shared and variant-specific assembly steps.
card_ideas.synthetic_question: Synthetic: Two process tracks each produce50units rather than one track100units. Can their learning curves be treated as identical?
card_ideas.synthetic_answer_key: Only if the relevant learning transfers. Separate common process steps from track-specific defects, product mix and die size.
card_ideas.new_constraint: New evidence:80% of process steps are shared but the remaining20% generate most defects.
